message.content:
**Answer:**  
The sculpture that most people associate with the 19th‑century art world is **Auguste Rodin’s “The Kiss” (1889)**. Created at the end of the century, it quickly became an icon of modern sculpture and remains one of the most reproduced and celebrated works from that period.  

While Rodin’s “The Thinker” would later become even more famous, its first public casts appeared only in the early 20th century (1902–03). Thus, within the strict bounds of the 1800s, “The Kiss” stands out as the definitive masterpiece of the era.
